seoTitle: How to Link PayPal to QuickBooks Online Easily
metaDescription: Link PayPal to QuickBooks Online as a bank feed or through Intuit's Connect to PayPal app. What each route imports, how the sign-in works, and how to avoid duplicate transactions.
intro:
QuickBooks Online can pull PayPal activity in automatically, so you categorise transactions instead of retyping them. There's more than one way to do it, though, and they don't import the same detail. Intuit documents three: PayPal Bank Feeds, the older Sync with PayPal app, and the Connect to PayPal app that Intuit describes as merging the other two.

The recording below uses the bank feed route: connect PayPal the way you'd connect a checking account, then review what lands in Bank transactions. That's the quickest setup. Its limit is that sales come through as summaries, without the fee and tax breakdown. If you need that detail, the app route in the last step is the one to use.
prerequisites: A QuickBooks Online subscription. Intuit lists the Connect to PayPal app for Simple Start, Essentials, Plus, Advanced and Solopreneur, and not for QuickBooks Self-Employed.
The PayPal login for the account's main holder. For the Connect to PayPal app, Intuit states that only the main PayPal user can grant permissions.

steps.heading: Start from the QuickBooks homepage
steps.body: Sign in and you land on the Business overview, with cards for bank balances, profit and loss and unpaid invoices. The bank connection flow starts from the Bank accounts card here or from the banking section of the menu. Jot down your current bank balance before connecting so you can sanity-check the numbers once PayPal activity arrives.

image.caption: The QuickBooks Online homepage, with the Bank accounts card that leads into the connection flow.

steps.heading: Search for PayPal on the connection screen
steps.body: Starting a new connection opens "Let's get a picture of your profits", with a name search and tiles for common banks such as Citi, Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo. PayPal isn't among the default tiles. Type PayPal into the search field and select it from the results.

image.caption: The "Let's get a picture of your profits" connection screen, with a search field above the grid of bank tiles.

steps.heading: Sign in to PayPal in the pop-up
steps.body: Selecting PayPal opens a separate window on PayPal's own site, so QuickBooks never handles your PayPal password. Sign in and approve the data-sharing request. If the window doesn't open, or you close it by accident, QuickBooks waits on a "Sign in to your account" screen with a Reopen window button. Click it to relaunch PayPal's sign-in without starting over.

image.caption: The waiting screen QuickBooks shows when the PayPal sign-in window hasn't opened, with a button to reopen it.

steps.heading: Review PayPal activity in Bank transactions
steps.body:
Once connected, PayPal activity shows up in Bank transactions for review, alongside your other accounts. Each row needs a customer or vendor and a category before you post it. QuickBooks suggests categories from your history, and where a transaction looks like one already in your books it offers a match. Take the match. Adding it again records the same money twice.

For sales, a bank feed gives you the summary amount only. PayPal's fee isn't broken out, so you'll need to record fees yourself or switch to the app route below. For repeating items, such as a customer's monthly payment, set up a bank rule so QuickBooks categorises them for you.

image.caption: The Bank transactions list with PayPal Transfer In rows among other deposits, each waiting for a customer and category before posting.

steps.heading: Or use the Connect to PayPal app for full sales detail
steps.body:
In QuickBooks, go to Integrations → Find integrations and search for Connect to PayPal. Intuit's help articles also call it the PayPal Connector by QuickBooks. Get the app, sign in with the main PayPal account's credentials, click Agree and Connect, and return to Intuit. You then pick the PayPal bank account in QuickBooks, a sales tax rate, and a start date for history.

Per Intuit's FAQ, the app imports up to 18 months of history (at setup only), syncs every 3 hours, supports more than one PayPal account, and doesn't support multi-currency. Fees on sales are pulled from PayPal and added when you match or add the transaction, not shown as separate lines. Pick the history start date carefully: Intuit warns that choosing dates already in your books can duplicate transactions.

troubleshooting.cause: The PayPal sign-in window didn't open, or was closed before you finished signing in.
troubleshooting.fix: Click Reopen window on the "Sign in to your account" screen to relaunch PayPal's sign-in without restarting the connection.

troubleshooting.cause: The same money was added from two sources, or the app's history start date overlapped transactions already entered. Intuit flags the second case directly.
troubleshooting.fix: Match feed items to existing transactions instead of adding them, and set the history start date after the last period you've already booked.

troubleshooting.problem: Connect to PayPal won't accept your login
troubleshooting.cause: Intuit states that only the main PayPal user can grant permissions; a secondary user login can't.
troubleshooting.fix: Have the PayPal account's main holder complete the connection.

troubleshooting.problem: Foreign-currency PayPal transactions don't come through correctly
troubleshooting.cause: The Connect to PayPal app doesn't support multi-currency transactions or reconciliation.
troubleshooting.fix: Handle those transactions manually, or compare the bank feed route in the table above.

faq.question: Which PayPal connection should I use?
faq.answer: If you only need to see money moving in and out, the bank feed is quickest. If you want each sale with its fee and tax, Intuit's Connect to PayPal app imports that detail and is the option Intuit positions as replacing the other two.

faq.question: Does QuickBooks see my PayPal password?
faq.answer: No. You sign in on PayPal's own page in a separate window, and QuickBooks receives only the authorised connection.

faq.question: How far back can I import PayPal transactions?
faq.answer: Intuit's Connect to PayPal FAQ says up to 18 months, chosen during the initial setup.

faq.question: How often do new PayPal transactions arrive?
faq.answer: The Connect to PayPal app imports every 3 hours, according to Intuit's FAQ.
